metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward bias by 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >30% from prior period), model overreacts and overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 10–15% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias toward prior 10–15 day average; use moving average of last 10 days as baseline for correction.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model tends to ignore long-term trend; if price has been rising for >10 days, add 3–5% upward bias to forecast horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period volatility; apply “tail correction”: add 2–5% to forecast if last 3–5 days show increasing variance or outlier events.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, model is likely underestimating supply/demand shock; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
